title: Polarity node — the one home (s238-D1)
description: A polarity is a permanent pull between two (or more) true things that is managed, never solved (s238-D4). It is a hyper-relational NODE with N typed parties and typed out-links to rulings; pairwise edges are DERIVED for consumers, never authored (s238-D1). This schema carries NO status field (s238-D3 / s237-D9: settled-by-obligation / resolved / open is derived at build time with a clock) and NO free-text judgement field of any name (s238-D7 refusal 3): the node's only judgement is a typed link to a knowledge/_rulings.json id. `additionalProperties: false` at every level is what makes refusals 3 and 5 structural rather than a list of banned words. Enforced by knowledge/_validate_polarities.py, which READS this file (the consumer's grammar) and never re-types its rules. PINNED (#239 lane F, V's Q2): the gate carries this file's sha256 and the floors of the five refusals in code — a schema edit must move the pin in the same commit, and a schema that LOOSENS a floor is refused (the floor is applied regardless); a schema may only TIGHTEN. THE RECEIPT (s240-D3, #242 lane P): every node traces to something Dave ruled, and the anchor is ONE POINTER PER NODE — either an R1 register row (`sources`, the migration's form) or, for a node born after R1, the knowledge/_rulings.json id that created it (`$seed`). Both on one node is refused, neither is refused. A RETIRED node KEEPS its row and carries `retiredBy` (the ruling id that retired it); it stays in this file and drops out of everything generated under _generated/.

id.description: pl-NN. The rename tension -> polarity happened before generation (s238-D4); the former tn-NN id is kept under sources[].id, never as an alias here.

parties.description: The things being pulled. Every ref MUST resolve against the live registers: a principle or obligation row in knowledge/brain/principles.json, a ruling id in knowledge/_rulings.json, or a declared stub in knowledge/brain/stubs.json (s238-D1; refusal 1). A party's KIND (principle / obligation / ruling / stub) is DERIVED from where the ref resolves — an obligation is a register row whose grade is L (s237-D1, s237-D2) — and is never typed here. The same ref may not appear twice on one node; a node may not be its own party; another polarity may not be a party.

ref.description: ASCII id of a principle / obligation (pr-…), a ruling (as spelled in _rulings.json) or a stub (st-…).

role.description: Which side of the pull the party stands on. Parties on the SAME side pull together (lane T finding 4: tn-19's three persuasion principles are one side) and produce no derived edge between them.

note.description: A VERBATIM gloss carried from the source row (e.g. the parenthetical after a principle id) — the gate checks it is a substring of the node's source row (#239 lane F, V's Q5); a note that is not verbatim is a judgement field (refusal 3). At most 15 words.

mediating_variable.description: The variable that decides which party wins in a given case — the thing that is MANAGED. Descriptive, carried VERBATIM from the source row (the gate checks the substring); at most 25 words (FLOATED figure, #239 lane F) — a paragraph here is a judgement (refusal 3).

links.description: Typed out-links to rulings ONLY (s238-D6: 'RULING LINKS ON A POLARITY ARE TYPED … the generator refuses an untyped one'). The four types and what each asserts, with the subject named because two of them are worded from the ruling's side: resolvedBy — the POLARITY is settled in this house by the ruling (its route is the ruling; lane T's R-RESOLVED); explainedBy — the RULING is explained by this polarity's principles (the s237-D5 relation: one-directional and advisory; a principle may explain a ruling and can never overturn one); challengedBy — the RULING is challenged by this polarity (advisory; the ruling stands until Dave rules; lane T finding 2 names tn-11 and tn-14); touches — the polarity and the ruling are adjacent and nothing stronger is claimed (the least claim; it never closes an open question). A fifth type is NOT ruled and is refused (refusal 2). A link to a principle, a stub or another polarity is refused (refusal 1): parties carry principles; edges are derived. A resolvedBy MUST carry a quote that VERIFIES against the node's source row (#239 lane F, V's Q3) — an unreceipted resolvedBy is a typed status by another door; touches may stay quote-free.

ref.description: A ruling id present in knowledge/_rulings.json and LIVE: not carrying `superseded_by`, not superseded in the store's prose, and — for a resolvedBy — not one whose status text says OPEN / PARKED / DEFERRED / FORKED (#239 lane F, V's Q1).

quote.description: The 3..15-word verbatim quote that justifies the TYPE — a receipt, not a judgement (refusal 3). Verified as a substring of the node's source row in the frozen R1 register; an unverifiable, empty or one-word quote is not a receipt.

$seed.description: THE BIRTH RECEIPT OF A NODE BORN AFTER R1 (s240-D3): the knowledge/_rulings.json id of the ruling that created this polarity. It is the ALTERNATIVE to `sources`, never its companion — the receipt is one pointer per node, so a node carrying both is refused (S-SOURCE) and so is a node carrying neither. An id that is not in knowledge/_rulings.json is R1-DANGLING. A $seed node claims no frozen R1 row, so the migration bijection is unaffected; it also has no source row, so it can carry no verifiable quote (a resolvedBy needs one — see x-refusals).

retiredBy.description: THE RETIREMENT RECEIPT (s240-D3): the knowledge/_rulings.json id of the ruling that retired this polarity. A retired node KEEPS its row here (and keeps its R1 `sources` claim, so no frozen row is orphaned) and DROPS OUT of everything generated under _generated/ — status rows, edges and the defaults declaration. A retired id still present in a generated file is R4-RETIRED-GENERATED. An id that is not in knowledge/_rulings.json is R1-DANGLING. Retirement is additive to the birth receipt: it is not the node's second receipt, it is the ruling that ended it.

sources.description: THE BIRTH RECEIPT OF A NODE THAT CAME FROM R1: the frozen register row that keeps the words this node does not carry (the_pull, how_it_resolves — ADR-0017: the node points, the source keeps the words). The path must be on the gate's source allow-list (today: the frozen R1 register only — a second register is Dave's), the id must be a row in it, and every frozen row is claimed by exactly one node (the migration receipt, verified). Not required (s240-D3): a node born after R1 carries `$seed` instead — exactly one of the two.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the source register (no spaces, no leading slash).

id.description: The row id inside that register (e.g. tn-01).

x-vocabulary: `maxWords` and `minWords` are house keywords (a standard validator ignores them; knowledge/_validate_polarities.py enforces them — words are counted after every Unicode format/control character is treated as a separator, so an invisible join cannot hide a paragraph). Everything else is draft 2020-12 core: type · required · additionalProperties · properties · items · enum · pattern · minItems · minLength.

x-refusals.description: The five refusals of s238-D7, named as the validator prints them. Listed here so the schema and the gate cannot describe two different contracts; the enforcement lives in knowledge/_validate_polarities.py. Sub-forms added #239 lane F are marked.
x-refusals.R1: a party or link ref — or (#242, s240-D3) a `$seed` / `retiredBy` receipt id — that does not resolve against the live registers (sub-forms: R1-DANGLING — also a resolvedBy to a ruling whose status text says OPEN/PARKED/DEFERRED/FORKED (#239) · R1-SUPERSEDED — the `superseded_by` field, or supersession in the store's prose (#239) · R1-SELF-PARTY · R1-CIRCULAR · R1-WRONG-REGISTER · R1-UNDECLARED-STUB)
x-refusals.R2: an untyped link (sub-forms: R2-UNTYPED — the key absent, null, or a link that is not an object (#239) · R2-UNKNOWN-TYPE)
x-refusals.R3: a judgement text field of any name on a node (sub-forms: R3-JUDGEMENT-FIELD — also a note / mediating_variable / stub phrase that is not verbatim in the frozen register, and free text at the top level (#239) · R3-QUOTE-TOO-LONG · R3-NOTE-TOO-LONG · R3-QUOTE-NOT-VERBATIM — also an empty, under-floor or unverifiable quote (#239) · R3-QUOTE-MISSING — a resolvedBy with no quote (#239))
x-refusals.R4: an authored edge file — pairwise edges exist only under _generated/ with a content-freshness check (sub-forms: R4-RETIRED-GENERATED — (#242, s240-D3) a node carrying `retiredBy` whose id still appears in a file under _generated/: a retired node keeps its row and drops out of everything generated · R4-AUTHORED-GENERATED — also a clock that is not ISO-8601 UTC, in the future, before the R1 asset, or differing across the three files (#239) · R4-AUTHORED-EDGES · R4-STRAY-FILE — every entry at every level is listed: dotfiles, schema/, _generated/, __pycache__, *.tmp, symlinks, a non-directory at a directory path (#239))
x-refusals.R5: a typed status on a node (R5-TYPED-STATUS)
x-refusals.S: the schema refusals the same grammar implies: S-PARSE (also a non-UTF-8 byte) · S-SHAPE (also the catch-all for any crash, named with its exception class and path; and an absent home in the source repo) · S-ID · S-MIN-PARTIES · S-ROLE · S-DUP-ID · S-DUP-PARTY · S-STUB-SHAPE · S-DUP-STUB · S-ONE-SIDED · S-SCHEMA (also a malformed schema) · S-FORMAT-CHAR (#239: a Unicode Cf/Cc/Co character in any string) · S-SOURCE (#239: a source path off the allow-list, an id that is not a row, a frozen row claimed twice or by no node; #242 s240-D3: a node carrying BOTH `sources` and `$seed` — the receipt is one pointer per node — or NEITHER) · S-RECEIPT (#239: the $migration receipt does not verify) · SCHEMA-PIN-MISMATCH (#239) · SCHEMA-LOOSENED (#239) · SCHEMA-KEYWORD-UNSUPPORTED · MISSING-GENERATED · STALE-GENERATED
